newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel trio sets blueprint for Thomson-CSF - paper.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel trio sets blueprint for Thomson-CSF - paper.

text.p: French engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom and allies Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation have drawn up a detailed blueprint for Thomson-CSF in the event they win control of the group in a relaunched privatisation, a French daily said on Tuesday.

Business newspaper La Tribune said ownership plans for the state electronics firm, which is being sold by private placement after the stalled privatisation of parent Thomson SA last year, were set out in a detailed accord in late January.
It said plans include a surprise takeover of Thomson-CSF missiles by Aerospatiale in return for part of its own capital.

Under the plan, Alcatel would take between 51-70 percent of Thomson-CSF, while privately-held Dassault Industries, the parent of Dassault Electronique and Dassault Aviation, would gain 10-12 percent, or up to 15 percent.
Aerospatiale, once merged with Dassault, would take seven to 10 percent of the capital, while 25 percent would be quoted on the Paris stock market. Employees would own around five percent.

Thomson-CSF would sell its missiles and missiles systems business, valued at four billion francs, to Aerospatiale, to allow it to compete with the Matra-BAe Dynamics joint venture between Lagardere and British Aerospace Plc.
La Tribune said this ran counter to previous expectations that Aerospatiale would transfer its missiles business to Thsomson-CSF, and not the other way round.
Alcatel had no immediate comment on the newspaper report.
Alcatel has floated an alliance with Aerospatiale and Dassault, which are due to merge, to try to strengthen its bid for Thomson-CSF against its rival Lagardere.
But the government is reported to want Alcatel and Lagardere to join forces in bidding for Thomson-CSF together to make a French national champion to confront U.S. competition.
La Tribune said the government would soon publish the conditions of sale for Thomson-CSF, perhaps on Thursday.
The French finance ministry declined comment.
